findings.where: First screen, Mark's photograph 'Mark M. Moseley at the lectern' (desktop right column; phone, below the margin notes), and the same photo in the motion specimen
findings.fault: The hero photograph has a wide, soft drop shadow, so it looks lifted off the page like a floating card. It is a static picture: clicking it does nothing. The article's photograph, the other exhibit on the page, sits flat with no shadow. So the same kind of object gets two treatments, and the shadow suggests the photo is either above the page or can be clicked.
findings.who_objects: A bank or agency visitor might take the lifted card for something to click, or as a stock web-template device. The founder asked for a journal-like page, and in a legal journal a plate lies flat on the paper. The house rule gives a shadow only to what floats or can be acted on.

findings.where: Article specimen, the 'Download' button on the document row 'Streamlining the PPP Process…' (desktop and phone), set against the first screen's 'Write to me' button
findings.fault: The page's two buttons look like they come from different systems. 'Write to me' is a square-cornered rectangle filled with blue. 'Download' is a rounded pill with a blue outline and an icon, and it is the only rounded shape anywhere on a page that is otherwise all square corners and hairlines.
findings.who_objects: Angélique, who will add more documents and needs one button style to copy. The founder judges the tile as one consistent look, and the pill reads like an app control dropped into a typeset page.

findings.where: Links across the page: the first-screen address 'Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com' (serif, ink, pale underline), the footer address (sans, house blue, blue underline), 'Replay the entrance' (sans, blue, underlined) and 'Download' (blue outline pill)
findings.fault: The same email address is styled two ways: in ink serif with a faint underline on the first screen, and in blue sans in the footer. The palette card says house blue marks links, yet the most important link on the page is the one that isn't blue. Overall, links come in three or four different looks.
findings.who_objects: A visitor learns from the footer and the replay link that blue underlined text is a link. The hero address, the one they most need, then reads more like body text than a link. The founder would also see the tile breaking its own palette rule.

findings.where: Photo captions: the hero caption (desktop and phone), set against the article caption 'A radio interview at the Belt and Road Summit. Placeholder: …' (desktop)
findings.fault: The two photos' captions are set differently. Under the hero photo, the italic serif caption and the sans placeholder note sit on separate lines. Under the article photo, they run together on one line at different sizes, and the line spacing is opened up to fit both, so the caption looks loose and patched together.
findings.who_objects: Angélique will copy the article caption as her template, and its mixed run-on line is the weaker of the two. A reader sees two caption styles on one page that is meant to be set like a journal.

findings.where: Motion specimen, the 'Replay the entrance' link (desktop)
findings.fault: The replay link floats near the centre of the page. It lines up with neither the text column's left edge (where the curve, the caption and the table start) nor the demo photograph above it.
findings.who_objects: The founder, reading the specimen as typeset work: one control left at an arbitrary position on a page where everything else hangs from the same left edge looks like a mistake.
